title: Scalar and strict quotient compatibility of the completed coefficient equivalence
statement: Let T and d be as in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. The completed coefficient ring pulled to the actual small Cech site is isomorphic to the inverse limit of the constant rings A/I^(n+1). The isomorphism preserves every scalar from A. There is an additive equivalence E from actual completed-coefficient module sheaves to module sheaves over this constant completed ring, naturally isomorphic to the fixed Cech module equivalence followed by restriction along the inverse ring isomorphism. The actual strict quotient-tower functor followed termwise by E is naturally isomorphic to E followed by the constant strict quotient-tower functor; at every level the comparison carries the specified actual quotient-unit map to the constant quotient-unit map.

source.place: current order 1316, Koszul-to-quotient comparison, including its unit equation

proof.text: Pull the finite constants comparison through the actual equivalence to the small site. Constant sheafification commutes with this equivalence. Naturality for each quotient transition gives an isomorphism of finite-ring systems. Its limit isomorphism identifies the completed rings and preserves scalars, since their finite projections coincide.

Use the ringed-site module equivalence, followed by scalar restriction along the completion isomorphism. Construct its natural identification with the fixed Cech module equivalence by the identity on underlying local sections.

Transport extension/restriction adjunctions across these equivalences. Uniqueness of left adjoints supplies each positive-quotient comparison. Its adjunction equation identifies the quotient units, whose local formulas are insertion of 1 into a tensor product.

The finite completion projections are locally surjective: on a covering, a section of a constant finite quotient is represented by an element of A/I^(n+1), which lifts to A. Thus each module quotient unit is epi. Cancelling these epis in the two natural quotient-unit squares proves compatibility with all quotient transitions. Assemble the level comparisons into the strict tower isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Formal comparison and unit-normalization details of the recorded Koszul/quotient reconstruction; proved from the existing universal and reflector interfaces.

theorem completed_constant_coefficient_equivalence
    (T : Scheme.{t}) {A : Type (t + 1)} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) :
    ∃ β : completedCechRing T d ≅
        ConstantCompletion.coefficients (completedCechTopology T) A d.ideal true,
      (∀ (U : (completedCechSite T)ᵒᵖ) (x : A),
        β.hom.hom.app U ((completedCechScalar T d x).val U) =
          (ConstantCompletion.algebraSection
            (ConstantCompletion.coefficientMap (completedCechTopology T) A d.ideal) x).val U) ∧
      ∃ E : reductionModules T (d.completedRing T) ≌ ConstantCompletion.Mod
          (ConstantCompletion.coefficients (completedCechTopology T) A d.ideal true),
        E.functor.Additive ∧
        Nonempty (E.functor ≅ (completedCechModulesEquiv T d).functor ⋙
          ConstantCompletion.res β.inv) ∧
        ∃ η : completedReductionModuleTowerFunctor T d ⋙
            (CategoryTheory.Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ _ _).obj E.functor ≅
              E.functor ⋙ ConstantCompletion.reductionTower
                (completedCechTopology T) A d.ideal true,
          ∀ (M : reductionModules T (d.completedRing T)) (n : ℕ),
            E.functor.map (((completedReductionModuleUnit d T).app M).app (op n)) ≫
                (η.hom.app M).app (op n) =
              ((ConstantCompletion.reductionUnit
                (completedCechTopology T) A d.ideal true).app (E.functor.obj M)).app (op n)
